To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the post-socialist transition in agriculture was characterized by de-collectivization, (b) de-collectivizing reforms in the Czech Republic were characterized by a relatively early, but gradual privatization of assets, and (c) the Czech agricultural sector has experienced an unprecedented process of de-collectivized agricultural restructuring and consolidation.

(1) the de-collectivization process in Czech and Slovak agriculture was not a result of the collapse of socialist institutions and the emergence of market institutions but was a result of the reorganization of the socialist institutions of the collective and state farms, and that (2) this reorganization was the result of an institutional change in the governance structure, namely, the change from the collective to the family farm.
the de-collectivization of Czech and Slovak farming was a process in which the state was a key player.

the socialist farm was not an efficient production unit because the incentives of the workers and managers were different from those of the owners.
